[reduced-length barrier for curves entering a surgery cap] Source: cao-zhu 1. Assertion (7.4.2)\group Canonical-Neighborhood Induction For any $L<\infty $ one can find $\bar{\delta }=\bar{\delta }(L,r,\widetilde{r}_m,\varepsilon )>0$ with the following property. Suppose that we have a curve $\gamma $, parametrized by $t\in [T_0,t_0]$, $(m-1)\varepsilon ^2\leq T_0<t_0$, such that $\gamma (t_0)=x_0$, $T_0$ is a surgery time, and $\gamma (T_0)$ lies in the gluing cap. Suppose also each $\delta $-cutoff surgery at a time in $[(m-1)\varepsilon ^2,\bar{T}]$ has $\delta \leq \bar{\delta }$. Then we have an estimate \begin{equation} \int ^{t_0}_{T_0}\sqrt{t_0-t}(R_+(\gamma (t),t) +|\dot{\gamma }(t)|^2)dt\geq L \end{equation} where $R_+=\max \{ R,0\} $.
